talk_track: Barry Hess here — I spent 16 years as CTO of a defense small business and fielded a patented tactical app platform with operators in theater, then watched it die force-wide for lack of a senior champion inside the building. Your Director of Engineering posting asks one person to 'drive the hard handoff from a thing that works in the lab to a thing that survives downrange and gets built at volume.' That line actually describes two jobs: an engineering leader can get you to volume, but survival downrange is decided in the program office, not on your 400-acre range. Weekly field tests prove the demo; the DoD valley of death opens after the demo lands, when months-to-field runs past the funded window. The companies that make the transition engineer the acquisition advocacy at the same time they engineer the product. Who owns the program-office side of that handoff today?
